History & Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
34-year-old active female marathon-in-training with 2-week history of activity-related right > bilateral knee pain and clicking, worsened by running/leg-extension exercises, evaluated via video consult; advised relative rest, ongoing ice, prescription NSAID, and referral to physiotherapy for full assessment and possible imaging.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Knee pain (predominantly right), clicking sensations.  
• Onset/Duration: Began ~2 weeks ago after increasing run distance (training 7–8 mile runs).  
• Course: Pain starts ≈20 min (~3 mi) into run; occasionally severe enough to stop running; improves with ice and rest; no baseline pain when walking, climbing stairs, or at rest.  
• Location/Character: Felt “in the middle” of right knee, sometimes shifting to right (lateral) side; occasional clicking during leg-extension/ab exercises.  
• Swelling: Single transient episode after first long run; resolved with ice; currently no visible swelling.  
• Neurologic: One episode of right-toe tingling post-run; resolved; no ongoing numbness or weakness.  
• Mechanical symptoms: Denies giving-way, locking, inability to fully flex/extend. Full ROM reported.  
• Aggravating factors: Running >20 min, leg-extension/ab exercises.  
• Relieving factors: Rest, ice, ibuprofen.  
• Associated/Pertinent negatives: No redness, heat, fever, calf pain, color change, persistent oedema, back pain, or other joint involvement.

Past Medical History:
• Hyperopia; status-post LASIK.  
• Severe UTI/possible renal colic in past (ER visit, no ongoing issues).  
• Remote right-knee contusion from ice-hockey fall (months ago), fully recovered.  
• Otherwise healthy; denies asthma, GERD, chronic GI issues.

Medications:
• Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN (dose/route/frequency per patient).  
• Aleve (naproxen) PRN – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Vitamin D – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Melatonin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Xanax (alprazolam) occasionally for sleep – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
• Highly physically active: ice hockey, regular gym workouts; currently marathon training (race in June).  
• Residence: 60 Sloane Avenue, London.  
• Tobacco: Not documented.  
• Alcohol: Not documented.  
• Recreational drugs: Occasional marijuana joint.  
• Occupation/other lifestyle details: Not documented.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (video consult).  
• Musculoskeletal (patient-reported/observed on video): No visible swelling, erythema, or deformity of knees. Able to fully flex/extend; no observable gait abnormality. No reported tenderness points tested.  
• Neurovascular: Normal color and temperature of lower legs per patient; sensation intact except for single resolved toe-tingling episode.  
(Comprehensive in-person exam deferred; physiotherapy referral planned.)

Investigations:
• None performed to date. Imaging to be considered after physiotherapy assessment.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Likely overuse-related anterior/lateral right knee pain most consistent with patellofemoral pain syndrome; alternate considerations include patellar tendinopathy and meniscal pathology. No red-flag features presently.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Patellofemoral pain syndrome – High likelihood: pain with running/leg extension, clicking, normal ROM, transient swelling.  
2. Patellar tendinopathy – Moderate: activity-related anterior knee pain; less clicking typical.  
3. Meniscal tear – Moderate: prior trauma and clicking support; absence of locking or persistent effusion argues against.

Issue 1 – Right knee pain/clicking (suspected patellofemoral pain syndrome):
• Continue ice therapy after activity.  
• Relative rest: reduce running mileage/intensity; avoid pain-provoking exercises.  
• Medication: Prescribed stronger NSAID (name/dose not specified in transcript) to be taken with food; avoid concurrent ibuprofen/naproxen.  
• Referral: Physiotherapy for detailed knee examination, gait assessment, strength/flexibility programme.  
• Contingency: If persistent or worsening swelling, warmth, redness, fever, mechanical locking, or inability to bear weight, patient to seek urgent medical review.  
• Possible imaging (MRI or X-ray) to be considered after physio review if symptoms persist or structural injury suspected.

Issue 2 – Intermittent right foot/toe paresthesia:
• Likely transient nerve irritation secondary to overuse; no active management required.  
• Monitor for recurrent or persistent numbness/weakness; report if occurs.

Issue 3 – NSAID use / GI safety:
• Counsel to take prescribed NSAID with meals; avoid duplicate OTC NSAIDs.  
• Warn regarding dyspepsia, black stools; stop and seek care if occur.  
• Consider PPI cover if prolonged course (not prescribed in session).

General plan items:
• Encourage gradual return-to-run programme once pain-free.  
• Maintain strength/flexibility programme per physiotherapist.  
• Follow-up: Arrange follow-up after physiotherapy report or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: Allergies, comprehensive vitals, full social & family history not obtained.  
• No direct conflict between transcript and DDx noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational noise but clinically adequate.
